(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Mr. Pasham Trivikram Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Mujeeb Kumar Sadasivuni, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the respondents.

2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of habeas corpus directing respondent No.3 to produce the detenu viz.,, Mohd. Sohail S/o late Mohd. Abdul Khader, now detained in Central Prison,
Chanchalguda, Hyderabad, and set aside the impugned detention order dated 14.12.2022 passed by respondent No.2 declaring it as illegal.

3. Respondent No.2 passed the detention order dated 14.12.2022 against the detenu under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers,
Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, KL,J & SKS,J Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders,

Mr. Pasham Trivikram Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the impugned detention order was issued without application of mind.
The detaining authority did not consider the entire material properly.
Therefore, there is no subjective satisfaction by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order.
Thus, the detention order is liable to be set aside.

7. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious and dangerous in nature.

The detaining authority considered the entire material placed, satisfied that the activities of the detenu were creating panic and a feeling of insecurity among the general public which were prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order'.

Having felt that the cases registered against him under the ordinary law have no deterrent effect in curbing his prejudicial activities, he is not amenable to ordinary law and with a view to prevent him from further indulging in such prejudicial activities, the detaining authority passed the detention order dated 14.12.2022 and the same was approved vide G.O.Rt.No.2362 of General Administration (Spl. Law & Order)
Department, dated 17.12.2022 by respondent No.1.
The acts of the KL,J & SKS,J detenu attract under the definition of a 'Goonda' as defined in Clause (g) of Section 2 of the Act No.1 of 1986.
Therefore, the detaining authority after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only, passed the detention order.
There is no error in it.
i) He has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. Union of India 1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh 2.

sentences.text:
Perusal of detention order, dated 14.12.2022, passed by respondent No.2 would reveal that the detaining authority passed the impugned detention order relying upon the aforesaid two (02)
crimes, which are serious and grave in nature.
The detaining authority has also referred the past history of detenu in commission of offences in two (02) crimes viz., Crime Nos.198 of 2019 and 250 of 2021.
Crime No.250 of 2021 was registered for the offences punishable under Section - 354D of IPC and Section - 11 read with 12 of POCSO Act.
In all the said crimes, on completion of investigation, the police laid the charge sheets and the Calendar Cases are pending for trial. .

(1988) 1 SCC 296 KL,J & SKS,J 9.

It is mentioned in the impugned detention order dated 14.12.2022 that the detenu has been habitually committing offences including attempt to murder and trespass using dangerous weapons in the limits of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate.
He has been causing widespread fear, terror and panic among the general public by committing such offences one after the other after enlarging on bail.

After release from judicial custody in Crime No.250 of 2021, there was no change in the attitude of the detenu in commission of offences and he committed the aforesaid crimes viz., Crime No.201 of 2022 and 269 of 2022.

Thus, the acts of the detenu would amply demonstrate his habitual nature of committing crimes and causing fear, panic and terror in the minds of general public and make his criminal history evident.
10.
The detaining authority further mentioned in the detention order that the detenu is an active and notorious rowdy sheeter and a desperate criminal.
It is also apt to refer that the detenu had committed different types of offences, which are grave and serious.
In one crime, he has attempted to kill with knife.
In other crime, he has trespassed, threatened the victim with knife.
In the past, he has committed theft of mobile phone by diverting the attention of the KL,J & SKS,J victim.
He has harassed a 14-year old girl.
All the said offences are serious and grave in nature.
The allegations are also serious.
The same will definitely disturb the 'public order' and created panic in the minds of general public.

Considering all the said aspects and also the aspect that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences which would detrimental to 'public order' and with a view to prevent him from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, the detaining authority arrived at the subjective satisfaction and passed the impugned detention order.
While passing the impugned detention order, the detaining authority considered that his acts are in the nature of 'goonda' as defined in clause - (g) of Section - 2 of the Act No.1 of 1986.

11. Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Chapter XXII of the IPC.
12.

The detaining authority also considered the nature of offences and the manner in which the same were committed.
Therefore, in order to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences passed the impugned detention order.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.
The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing.

14. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4, the Apex Court held as under:
"...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some?

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities .
AIR 1966 SC 740 KL,J & SKS,J and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.
A District Magistrate is entitled to take action under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances.

It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order".
One has to imagine three concentric circles.
Law and order represents the largest circle within which is the next circle representing public order and the smallest circle represents security of State.
It is then easy to see that an act may affect law and order but not public order just as an act may affect public order but not security of the State."

15. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 5, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not .

sentences.text: (1984) 3 SCC 14 KL,J & SKS,J characterize as an act of 'habitual'.

The Apex Court was of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general.

16. As discussed above, in the aforesaid crimes, which were relied upon by the detaining authority,
the police seized the knife used in commission of offences.
All the said cases are pending for trial.
It is also to be noted about the modus operandi of the detenu in committing similar offences repeatedly and such acts would attract under the definition of 'Goonda'.

4 while invoking the powers under the Act No.1 of 1986, has to consider the entire material on record and come to a subjective satisfaction that due to the acts committed by the detenu, nature of offences and the manner in which the same were committed would disturb the public order.

sentences.text: To prevent the detenu from committing the similar offences, the detaining authority shall issue preventive detention order against the detenu.
This Court has to consider facts and circumstances of each case on case to case basis.
KL,J & SKS,J 17.
There is no dispute with regard to the legal proposition that the detention order shall be issued in rarest of rare cases, that too, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offences.
Article - 21 of the Constitution of India enshrined the detenu the fundamental right of personal liberty which is precious right enshrined to the citizens as per the Constitution of India.
At the same time, duty cast upon the 'State' as defined under Article - 12 of the Constitution of India to maintain law and order as well as public order.
When there is disturbance causes to the public order, it is the duty of the 'State' to invoke the procedure laid down under the Act No.1 of 1986, to prevent detenu from committing similar offences.

18. As discussed above, the facts of the present case would reveal that the detenu is having criminal history and the allegations levelled against him in the aforesaid two (02) crimes are serious and grave in nature including attempt to murder and trespass and threatening the victim on the point of knife.
Certainly, the acts of the detenu in commission of the aforesaid offences disturb the 'public order' and the impact of the said offences would create panic in the minds of the public.
The detaining authority having considered all the said aspects arrived at the subjective satisfaction and passed the KL,J & SKS,J impugned detention order.

Therefore, viewed from any angle, we are of the considered view that there is no error in the impugned detention order dated 14.12.2022 passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential approval order vide G.O.Rt.No.2362, dated 17.12.2022.
Thus, the writ petition fails and the same is liable to be dismissed.
19. The present writ petition is accordingly dismissed.
In the circumstances of the cases, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in the writ petition shall stand closed.
